title: Blink LED
description: Verify the USB path, board profile, bootloader, compile, upload, and sketch execution.
notes: Verify the onboard L LED, not the always-on power LED.
boundary: This verifies the programming path only; it is not a sensor measurement.

title: Synthetic Signal
description: Generate a 0.5 Hz sine wave at 50 Hz to verify Arduino → serial → BetterBoard → measurement export without a sensor.
notes: No external sensor is required.
boundary: Synthetic data validates the software path, not experimental accuracy.

title: Bench 01 — Analog Control & Instrumentation
description: Turn a potentiometer or other known-safe low-voltage analog source into a complete input → ADC → filtering → PWM command → live measurement workflow.
hardware: potentiometer or known-safe low-voltage analog source on A0
optional LED with suitable series resistor on PWM pin D9
notes: Built-in LED turns on above 50% normalized input.
D9 outputs a 0–255 PWM command proportional to the calibrated normalized input.
The reported voltage is nominal until the real ADC reference/input path is characterized.
boundary: Use only inputs within the board's supported analog range. Nominal voltage, filtering, and endpoint scaling do not by themselves establish calibration accuracy or traceability.

title: Bench 03 — Embedded Numerical Reliability
description: Run the Numerical Error Analysis Taylor recurrence on the real MCU and capture parameter-scan, convergence, cancellation, stopping-rule, timing, and floating-point-environment evidence.
notes: No external sensor is required.
study_code 1 is the x-parameter scan; study_code 2 is fixed-term convergence at x=80.
method_code 0 is raw Taylor; method_code 1 is range-reduced Taylor.
Use scripts/bench03_embedded_numerical.py for reference-based accuracy, ULP, false-convergence, and reliability decisions.
boundary: The MCU can establish its arithmetic result, stopping behavior, cancellation indicator, timing, and reported floating-point environment, but it cannot establish reference accuracy by itself. Host-oracle analysis remains a separate evidence step.

title: Magnet Bench 01 — Vector Field Acquisition
description: Acquire the complete lab-frame magnetic-field vector from an MLX90393 at 20 Hz, preserving Bx, By, Bz, derived vector magnitude |B|, and a primary axis for downstream characterization and RADIA comparison.
hardware: ordinary small permanent magnet / magnetic test object
notes: Default primary axis is Z.
Bmag_uT is derived as sqrt(Bx^2 + By^2 + Bz^2).
The firmware intentionally does not subtract ambient/background field; Magnet Bench 02 handles baseline evidence explicitly.
Control sensor orientation, scan path, coordinate origin, polarity and distance reference for comparisons.
boundary: This measures magnetic field at the sensor location/orientation. It does not define an intrinsic magnet strength, establish calibration traceability, prove model validity, or guarantee that the sensor is unsaturated.

title: 3-axis Acceleration
description: Acquire ax, ay, az and a configurable primary axis from an ADXL345 at 100 Hz.
hardware: ADXL345 accelerometer or a later confirmed compatible replacement
notes: Default primary axis is Z.
The user's photographed XYZ module has not yet been confirmed as ADXL345.
boundary: Mechanical-honeycomb measurements are an analogue experiment, not direct graphene validation.

title: Photogate Timer
description: Timestamp falling-edge events, reject very close duplicate edges, and report period and frequency.
notes: Uses INPUT_PULLUP and a falling-edge interrupt on D2.
Minimum edge spacing is 2 ms in the canonical firmware.
boundary: Frequency accuracy depends on the sensor, geometry, event definition, and clock behavior.

title: Quadrature Encoder
description: Track quadrature counts on D2/D3 and convert counts to angle at 100 Hz.
notes: COUNTS_PER_REVOLUTION=600 is a placeholder and must match the actual encoder.
boundary: Angle is only calibrated when counts-per-revolution and mechanical coupling are known.

title: Pulse / RPM
description: Measure pulse periods and convert them to RPM using a configurable pulses-per-revolution constant.
notes: PULSES_PER_REVOLUTION defaults to 1 and must be configured for the real sensor.
boundary: RPM accuracy depends on pulses-per-revolution and sensor/event quality.

title: Random Walk Robot
description: Run conservative, bounded stochastic low-speed commands for a two-motor tabletop robot.
hardware: two small low-voltage DC gear motors
physical_lab_targets: Random Walk & Monte Carlo physical experiment
notes: Motor-driver pin assignments are placeholders until the exact driver is identified.
Actual x(t), y(t) should come from independent position measurement such as camera/object tracking.
boundary: Motor command duration is not a measured trajectory or displacement.

title: I²C Scanner
description: Scan 7-bit I²C addresses to help identify whether a connected I²C device responds.
notes: Diagnostic output is intentionally textual and should not be registered as Measurement Evidence.
boundary: An address response identifies bus communication only; it does not prove the exact sensor model or correct calibration.

title: Numerical Error — Step-size Differentiation
description: Sweep h for forward and central differentiation of sin(x) on the MCU to expose truncation-to-roundoff behavior.
notes: MCU cosf(x) is a convenient onboard comparison; a high-precision host oracle remains the stronger accuracy reference.
boundary: This is a numerical-method experiment. MCU library output is not an exact mathematical oracle.

title: Numerical Error — Catastrophic Cancellation
description: Compare sqrt(1+x)-1 with its algebraically equivalent stable form as x becomes small.
notes: The two formulas are mathematically equivalent but not equally stable in finite precision.
boundary: Formula disagreement demonstrates finite-precision sensitivity; use a host oracle for exact error attribution.

title: Numerical Error — Accumulation & Kahan Sum
description: Compare naive repeated addition with Kahan compensated summation under the same AVR floating-point environment.
notes: The printed target is still float arithmetic; BetterBoard host analysis can supply a higher-precision decimal reference.
boundary: The experiment compares accumulation algorithms and runtime; the MCU-computed target is not an exact oracle.

title: Numerical Error — MPU6050 Integration
description: Acquire real MPU6050 acceleration/gyro data and compare rectangle and trapezoidal gyro integration on the same discrete samples.
notes: Gyroscope bias and noise are measurement effects; rectangle-vs-trapezoid disagreement is a numerical-method effect on the same samples.
boundary: Integrated angle is not absolute orientation truth unless sensor bias, alignment, timing and an independent reference are characterized.
